title: New Year Tree Decorations
statementMd:
Due to atheistic Soviet past, Christmas wasn't officially celebrated in Russia for most of the twentieth century. As a result, the Russian traditions for Christmas and New Year mixed into one event celebrated on the New Year but including the tree, a Santa-like 'Grandfather Frost', presents and huge family reunions and dinner parties all over the country. Bying a Tree at the New Year and installing it in the house is a tradition. Usually the whole family decorates the tree on the New Year Eve. We hope that Codeforces is a big and loving family, so in this problem we are going to decorate a tree as well.

So, our decoration consists of $*n*$ pieces, each piece is a piece of colored paper, its border is a closed polyline of a special shape. The pieces go one by one as is shown on the picture. The $*i*$-th piece is a polyline that goes through points: $(0, 0)$, $(0, *y*_{0})$, $(1, *y*_{1})$, $(2, *y*_{2})$, ..., $(*k*, *y*_{*k*})$, $(*k*, 0)$. The width of each piece equals $*k*$.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/974c60d3c0398068e21a38010023bfe6a6de7430.png) The figure to the left shows the decoration, the figure to the right shows the individual pieces it consists of.

The piece number 1 (shown red on the figure) is the outer piece (we see it completely), piece number 2 (shown yellow) follows it (we don't see it completely as it is partially closed by the first piece) and so on. The programmers are quite curious guys, so the moment we hung a decoration on the New Year tree we started to wonder: what area of each piece can people see?

## Input

The first line contains two integers, $*n*$ and $*k*$ $(1 ≤ *n*, *k* ≤ 300)$. Each of the following $*n*$ lines contains $*k* + 1$ integers — the description of the polyline. If the $*i*$-th line contains ontegers $*y*_{*i*, 0}, *y*_{*i*, 1}, ..., *y*_{*i*, *k*}$, that means that the polyline of the $*i*$-th piece goes through points $(0, 0)$, $(0, *y*_{*i*, 0})$, $(1, *y*_{*i*, 1})$, $(2, *y*_{*i*, 2})$, ..., $(*k*, *y*_{*i*, *k*})$, $(*k*, 0)$ $(1 ≤ *y*_{*i*, *j*} ≤ 1000)$.

## Output

Print $*n*$ real numbers — for each polyline, the area of its visible part.

The answer will be considered correct if its relative or absolute error do not exceed $10^{ - 4}$.
statementZhMd:
由于无神论的苏联历史，圣诞节在二十世纪的大部分时间里并未在俄罗斯正式庆祝。因此，俄罗斯的圣诞节和新年传统逐渐融合成一个在新年庆祝的节日，其中包括圣诞树、类似圣诞老人的“严寒爷爷”、礼物，以及遍布全国的盛大家庭团聚和晚宴。在新年购买一棵树并将其装饰在家中是一项传统。通常，整个家庭会在除夕装饰圣诞树。我们希望 Codeforces 是一个团结而充满爱的大家庭，所以在这道题中，我们也要装饰一棵树。

我们的装饰由 $*n*$ 个部件组成，每个部件都是一张彩纸，其边界是一条特殊形状的闭合折线。这些部件按照图片所示依次排列。第 $*i*$ 个部件是一条依次经过以下点的折线：$(0, 0)$、$(0, *y*_{0})$、$(1, *y*_{1})$、$(2, *y*_{2})$、...、$(*k*, *y*_{*k*})$、$(*k*, 0)$。每个部件的宽度等于 $*k*$。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/974c60d3c0398068e21a38010023bfe6a6de7430.png) 左图展示了整个装饰，右图展示了它所包含的各个部件。

编号为 1 的部件（图中以红色表示）位于最外层（我们可以完整看到它），编号为 2 的部件（图中以黄色表示）紧随其后（由于部分区域被第一个部件遮挡，我们无法完整看到它），依此类推。程序员们都非常好奇，因此，当我们把装饰挂到新年树上的那一刻，就开始思考：人们能够看到每个部件的面积是多少？

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*k*$ $(1 ≤ *n*, *k* ≤ 300)$。接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，每行包含 $*k* + 1$ 个整数，用于描述一条折线。如果第 $*i*$ 行包含整数 $*y*_{*i*, 0}, *y*_{*i*, 1}, ..., *y*_{*i*, *k*}$，这表示第 $*i*$ 个部件的折线依次经过点 $(0, 0)$、$(0, *y*_{*i*, 0})$、$(1, *y*_{*i*, 1})$、$(2, *y*_{*i*, 2})$、...、$(*k*, *y*_{*i*, *k*})$、$(*k*, 0)$ $(1 ≤ *y*_{*i*, *j*} ≤ 1000)$。

## 输出格式

输出 $*n*$ 个实数，分别表示每条折线对应部件的可见部分面积。

如果答案的相对误差或绝对误差不超过 $10^{ - 4}$，则认为答案正确。
